logline: A villager kid lives behind a 40-block wall that old Tomas raises every morning; the morning Tomas is too tired, the kid climbs it for him.
question: why tf is the village wall forty blocks high with no gate?
premise: A village sits inside a stone-brick wall 40 blocks high with no gate. Every dawn a little dirt pokes over the rim from outside, and old Tomas, the mason, climbs up and builds one block higher above it. A block of the wall once vanished; Tomas patched it by noon. Tomas is the only one who has been outside: he came in an old minecart before the wall, and he hides when the kids push it. He says there's nothing out there 'we want to trade with'.
twist: The thing outside is a player. The brown 'plant' is his dirt pillar (he towers up every morning to look in; Tomas builds one higher to stay above it), the vanished block is the one he mined to peek, the minecart is how players move villagers, and outside the wall is his trading hall: a hundred villagers, each boxed in a one-block cell. One morning Tomas is too tired to climb, so the kid goes up for him and SAYS what he sees: a man standing on the brown plant, a hundred of us behind him, each in a tiny box. The man looks up and puts down one more. The wall was never for monsters; it's a race to stay hidden from him.

lines.text: The WALL / around my village / is FORTY blocks high. / And nobody will tell me WHY.
lines.say: The wall around my village is forty blocks high. And nobody will tell me WHY.
lines.note: one bright breath on the fact, then the question, curious, not scared: the viewer's why, said out loud (docs/story_format.md beat 1)

lines.text: Old TOMAS adds / ONE more / every MORNING.
lines.say: Old Tomas adds one more every MORNING.

lines.text: A ZOMBIE / can't even jump / TWO blocks. / So we're SUPER safe!
lines.say: A zombie can't even jump two blocks. So we're super SAFE!
lines.note: delighted, doing the maths, totally sure

lines.text: There's no GATE. / Who NEEDS one? / Everything's IN here.
lines.say: There's no gate. Who needs one? Everything's in HERE.

lines.text: Once, a BLOCK / just VANISHED. / Blocks DO that, / I guess. / Tomas had it BACK / by NOON.
lines.say: Once, a block just vanished. Blocks do that, I guess. Tomas had it back by NOON.
lines.note: a shrug on the middle part, then proud of Tomas

lines.direction: slow and low, still facing the patched block

lines.text: Every MORNING, / something BROWN / grows over the TOP. / Like a little PLANT!
lines.say: Every morning, something brown grows over the top. Like a little PLANT!
lines.note: charmed by it, a fun fact; the kid never says dirt (the picture shows it)

lines.text: So old Tomas / climbs up / and builds one HIGHER. / He ALWAYS wins.
lines.say: So old Tomas climbs up and builds one higher. He always WINS.
lines.note: proud, like it's a game Tomas plays with the plant

lines.text: Tomas came here / in that old MINECART. / Like a KING!
lines.say: Tomas came here in that old minecart. Like a KING!
lines.note: impressed, the coolest fact about him

lines.text: When the kids PUSH it, / Tomas runs and HIDES. / He's the BEST / at hide and SEEK.
lines.say: When the kids push it, Tomas runs and hides. He's the best at hide and SEEK.

lines.text: I ASKED him / what's OUT there.
lines.say: I asked him what's out THERE.

lines.text: Nothing we want / to TRADE with.
lines.say: Nothing we want to TRADE with.
lines.direction: old and slow, closing the subject, kind but final

lines.text: But THIS morning, / old Tomas / was too TIRED / to get up.
lines.say: But this morning, old Tomas was too tired to get UP.
lines.note: soft, worried for him the way a kid is for a grandpa; not scared of anything else

lines.text: So I took his BRICK / and climbed up FOR him. / Maybe I'd see / a real MONSTER!
lines.say: So I took his brick and climbed up for him. Maybe I'd see a real MONSTER!
lines.note: brave for Tomas, then thrilled, speeding up as he climbs; excited, never scared

lines.text: A MAN / was standing on the brown PLANT, / and behind him / were a HUNDRED of us, / each in a tiny BOX.
lines.say: A man was standing on the brown plant, and behind him were a hundred of us, each in a tiny BOX.
lines.note: THE REVEAL (docs/story_format.md beat 6): one plain sentence, what the kid SEES, still bright and curious, not afraid; the viewer makes the one jump (the plant was him; the boxes are for us)

lines.text: He looked UP at me, / and put down / ONE more.
lines.say: He looked up at me, and put down one MORE.
lines.note: the one beat after the reveal: level, bright, a new person; echoes L02's 'ONE more' (the race the wall is for); cut about 1 s after 'MORE'
